public_rationale: GPT-4.5 was a documented counterexample before the post. OpenAI reported improved performance from scaling unsupervised learning and explicitly distinguished the model from models that think before responding. This contradicts the assertion that extra inference-time reasoning was the only successful route to improving new models.
limitations: The decisive evaluations are developer-reported rather than an independent replication.
The evidence does not show that non-reasoning models improved on every task or matched the strongest reasoning models.
The report does not isolate every training change through controlled ablations.

criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one new non-reasoning model demonstrably improves on its predecessor through training or another method that does not require extra inference-time reasoning.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI explicitly describes GPT-4.5 as not thinking before responding and attributes gains to unsupervised scaling. Its reported comparisons include GPQA scores of 71.4% versus 53.6% for GPT-4o, providing a counterexample to the claim that additional inference-time reasoning was the only route to improvement.
